newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power dips amid warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power dips amid warmer weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. eased Friday, after rising steadily for most of this week, due largely to expected warmer weather, market sources said.
The drop came despite the partial outage late Thursday of a California nuclear unit and a lack of surplus power sales by the Bonneville Power Administration over the weekend through Monday.
"It's warming up (in the Pacific Northwest) again," said one trader. "If Bonneville comes back into the market, prices should come down again."
In addition to warmer temperatures, traders said weaker natural gas prices following the end-October target for winter storage purchases were putting a damper on power prices.
"The whole energy complex is coming down--everything was way overvalued," noted another trader.
Firm on-peak California-Oregon border (COB) prices for Saturday were quoted $24.50-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), while Monday quotes were $25.00-25.50, compared with $26.00 on Thursday.
Firm on-peak Mid-Columbia was quoted $22.50-23.00, compared with $23.50-24.00 on Thursday.
Output from the 1,080-megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was cut to 46 percent Thursday evening after a control rod was dislodged.
But the unit was back to 56 percent by early Friday and expected to reach full power by early Saturday.
Meanwhile, the 1,221-MW unit 1 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant in Arizona continued to ramp up after being shut September 21 for refueling. It was at 40 percent power mid-day Friday.
But another Southwest power plant, the 720-MW unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired plant in Page, Ariz., is scheduled to shut next Saturday until December 18 for maintenance.
In addition, the 360-MW unit 1 at the San Juan coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was taken off line early Wednesday for unplanned repairs.
A time estimate for its restart was not yet available.
Next-day Palo Verde firm peak power was quoted near $23.00 per MWh, little changed from Thursday.
Next-day firm peak prices at Four Corners were said to be near Palo Verde quotes.
Cash Palo Verde for the balance of November was quoted $22.00-23.73, while Mid-Columbia was offered at $24.25 and COB was offered at $25.50. December COB was reported to trade at $22.90.
